memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Moses brought their case before the LORD, and the LORD said to him, "What Zelophehad's daughters are saying is right. You must certainly give them property as an inheritance among their father's relatives and give their father's inheritance to them." - Num 27:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses does not simply decide the matter himself. He brings the sisters' case before the Lord, seeking God's own judgment. And God's answer is clear and gracious: what these daughters are saying is right. They must certainly be given the inheritance they requested. God upholds their cause.

What a beautiful revelation of God's character. He listens to the appeal of five otherwise unnamed women in a vast nation, and He declares their request just. God is not indifferent to those the world might overlook. He hears the cry for fairness and responds with what is right. His justice extends to all His people, great and small.

There is also wisdom in Moses' example. Faced with a difficult question, he took it to the Lord rather than relying on his own judgment. When we do not know what is right, the wisest course is to bring the matter to God and seek His will. He gives wisdom generously to those who ask.

This is the God we know in Christ, one who welcomes the humble, hears the overlooked, and always does what is right. In Him there is neither favouritism nor injustice; all are precious in His sight (Gal 3:28). Bring your questions and concerns to this God, confident that He listens and judges justly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God hears even those the world overlooks?
2. When facing hard decisions, do you bring them to God as Moses did?
3. How does God's justice toward these women encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You hear even those the world overlooks and always do what is right. When I face hard decisions, help me bring them to You and trust Your just and gracious answer. Amen.
